officialFacts.text: Under NAMASTE Scheme, Union Minister of State Shri B. L. Verma Distributes PPE Kits And Ayushman Cards To Safai Mitras In Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh

Under the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) Scheme of Union Ministry of Social Justice And Empowerment, a major programme for the distribution of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) kits and Ayushman Cards, was organised at Peeli Kothi Civil Lines area, in Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh, today.

example.heading: Illustration
example.text: Illustration: If an urban local body profiles sanitation workers and links each verified worker to PPE and health protection, it can make welfare delivery more targeted; the source does not establish that every such system functions effectively in practice.

pocketRead.excerpt: On 27 October 2026, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment reported NAMASTE-linked distribution of PPE kits and Ayushman Cards to Safai Mitras in Moradabad.

question.answer: The approach is useful because profiling identifies the intended beneficiaries, PPE addresses immediate occupational exposure, and Ayushman Cards provide a health-protection link. Durable results still require mechanised cleaning, training, enforcement and local monitoring; the reported distribution alone cannot prove elimination of hazardous work.
question.prompt: How can NAMASTE move beyond benefit distribution to improve the dignity and safety of sanitation workers?

sections.heading: What the reported action shows
paragraphs: On 27 October 2026, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment reported a Moradabad programme under NAMASTE involving PPE kits and Ayushman Cards for Safai Mitras. The source identifies safety, health and social security as the programme’s focus.
The source reports 90,194 verified sewer and septic tank workers, 88,222 provided PPE kits and 80,180 covered through Ayushman Cards. It also reports 3,36,492 waste pickers profiled nationally. [5]

sections.heading: Why implementation matters
paragraphs: The mechanism is sequential: profiling helps identify workers, PPE can reduce exposure during work, and health insurance can reduce the financial burden of illness. The scheme’s official description also includes training and mechanised sanitation, which are necessary because equipment distribution alone does not remove hazardous work.

A practical limitation is that the report does not establish regular PPE use, quality of equipment, mechanisation outcomes or reduction in accidents. Monitoring must therefore examine outcomes, not only distribution numbers.

staticDefinition: NAMASTE is the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem, a scheme associated with the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment that seeks safer and more dignified sanitation work through worker profiling and linked interventions such as PPE, health protection, training and mechanisation. [1]
use: Use NAMASTE to connect welfare delivery, occupational safety, dignity of labour, urban governance and ethical public administration in answers on vulnerable sections and social justice.

advisory_notes: “Ethical public administration” is a reasonable GS4 application, but it is an analytical linkage rather than a direct syllabus phrase.
“Social security” is broader than the supplied report’s specific PPE and Ayushman Card measures; retain it as framing or qualify it as health protection.
“Profiling can make a historically informal workforce more visible” is sound analysis, but the supplied report does not establish that the workforce is informal.
“Portability of benefits” and “personal-data protection” are useful implementation recommendations, but they are not evidenced in the supplied PIB extract.
“Elimination of hazardous work” is a policy objective supported by the scheme’s official description, but the Moradabad report itself establishes only distribution and coverage, not elimination.
The numerical figures in the pocketRead are transcribed consistently with the supplied PIB extract; no arithmetic error is apparent.
The hypothetical worker-profiling example is clearly labelled as an illustration and appropriately avoids asserting that such a system works effectively in practice.
The proposed GS2 anchor and GS2.6/GS2.7 codes are substantively relevant; GS4.5 is defensible as an applied ethics linkage, though the core tagging is stronger under GS2.

wayForward: Complete worker profiling while protecting personal data and ensuring portability of benefits.
Make PPE quality, fit, replacement, training and regular use subject to safety audits.
Prioritise mechanised cleaning and strengthen emergency response and municipal accountability.
Track outcomes such as unsafe-entry incidents, training completion, health access and grievance resolution rather than only distribution totals.
